messages:
nina: Quick heads-up — onboarded orthopy-2b embeddings into staging. Ran a default holdout (10k queries). int8 per-tensor w/ postnorm -> recall@10 down ~3.7% vs fp16. Curious if this is a quant pattern or preprocessing issue.

aj: Can you paste the eval command + a tiny metric table so we can reproduce?

nina: Sure. Command I ran:
```
eval_holdout --model=orthopy-2b --quant=int8 --quant-mode=per-tensor --preprocess=postnorm --k=10 --queries=10000
```
Rough metrics I got (rounded):
```
FP16 recall@10: 0.882
INT8 (per-tensor) recall@10: 0.845
INT8 (per-channel) recall@10: 0.873
cosine avg sim shift: -0.012
centroid shift (L2): 0.09
```
Numbers are from a single holdout run.

ben: UMAP looks permuted vs fp16 — clusters elongated and tails stretched. Posted image: http://img.internal/orthopy/umap-int8.png :thinking_face:

sophia: Per-channel quant helped a lot here. Did you try pre-normalize -> quantize -> post-normalize? That often reduces centroid drift on contrastive-trained models.

nina: Tried that: pre-normalize + per-channel -> recall@10: 0.879. Still ~-0.3% vs fp16 but much closer. Pre-normalize = L2 unit norm before cast.

michael: What's the batch size during infer? Microbatching/fused kernels can change final vector distribution in some runtimes.

nina: batch_size=64, microbatch mode=auto on the staging runner. I'll run batch_size=16/32/64 sweep to check.

kate: Also try covariance whitening with a tiny ridge (eps=1e-3) after quantization. That fixed centroid mean-shift for us on a different model.

ops-bot: CI: embed-evals/orthopy-run-174 — baseline fp16 ✅, int8 per-tensor ❌ (recall drop >3%), int8 per-channel ⚠️ (minor gap). Full logs: https://ci.redwood/orthopy/174

aj: Can we add a quick A/B to route 10% traffic to per-channel int8 in dedicated trial? Want to capture latency/cost and live recall proxies.

nina: +1. I'll spin a canary config: route 10% -> orthopy-2b-int8-perchannel, keep rest fp16. Action items from here: (1) run batch_size sweep (16,32,64) with pre-normalize+per-channel, (2) try whitening+ridge post-quant, (3) run small A/B canary in dedicated and collect latency/cost + eval holdouts. I'll post results in this thread.

ben: +1 :thumbsup:

sophia: If you want, I can add a tiny synthetic that stresses near-duplicate queries to see if recall gap widens.

nina: please do — add to the holdout and tag me. Thanks everyone.
